title: Stop hook tells the reader to run /in-finish at the end of every turn
body:
AE found this on 3.5.2. intent-vc gave it to dc for the b353 batch.

Claude Code runs the Stop hook at the end of each turn, not at the end of a session. When the tree has uncommitted paths, `session-finish` prints "Session wrap-up reminder: N uncommitted path(s). Run /in-finish to update ST docs, intent/wip.md, and prepare a clean commit." after every such turn. `/in-finish` commits. In AE's course the attendee reviews and commits by hand, so the advice is wrong for that reader at every turn.

Fix: the hook names the uncommitted paths (the first few, then a count of the rest) and gives no instruction. `/in-finish` stays a session-end step, which the skill and CLAUDE.md already say. A clean tree, and a tree that git cannot read, show nothing. The docs that say the Stop hook reminds the reader to run `/in-finish` change to match.
